newsitem.title: UK: Hitachi Credit(UK) plans London stock market float.
newsitem.headline: Hitachi Credit(UK) plans London stock market float.

text.p: Credit finance company Hitachi Credit (UK) PLC (HCUK) is to seek a full listing by way of an institutional placing on the London Stock Exchange in summer 1997, and UBS Limited will act as sponsor and broker to the issue, it said on Monday.
In the first ever Japanese initial public offering (IPO), the company is expecting to have a capitalistaion of between 45-50 million stg and expecting to raise 15-20 million stg.

HCUK offers a range of finacial products for both the business and personal sectors in the UK and is at present a wholly owned subsidiary of Hitachi Credit Corporation of Japan (HCC) which is in turn 52.4 percent owned by Hitachi Ltd.
The statement said that following flotation, HCC intends to maintain ownership of approximately 60 percent of HCUK.
"The flotation offers HCUK access to additional capital to take advatage of opportunites to grow organically and by appropriate acquisitions," said David Anthony general manager in a statement.
"Wherever possible we lend to the customers of well regarded manufacturers and retailers with whom we have established relationships," he added.
Activities of the HCUK group of companies include isurance, business and retail credit as well as contract hire and fleet management.

Based in Hounslow in south-east England, HCUK made pre-tax profits of 3.7 million stg on turnover of 51.9 million stg for the year ending on March 1996. This is an increase of 34 percent on 1995 pre-tax profit of 2.7 million stg and an increase of 15 percent on 1995 turnover of 44.9 million stg.

For the six months to 30 September 1996 the HCUK group made a pre-tax profit of 2.2 million stg on turnover of 28.3 million stg which is up 21 percent and 11 percent respectively on the corresponding period to 30 September 1995.
The HCUK group of companies had assets of around 300 million stg at 31 March 1996.
